sources.citation: VanBib: A database of references to resources on Vanuatu languages, v1.3 (Zenodo, 2025).
sources.note: 19 Bierebo entries (Budd 2009, 2010, 2005; Tryon 1976, 1986; Crowley 1991; Early 2004; ABVD/ACD/ASJP wordlists); the only 'phonology' item is Tryon 1986 (consonant mutation). Files Fraser 1891 under both bier1244 and bier1246 Bieria.

sources.citation: ABVD wordlists Bierebo (Bonkovia) id 1041, Bierebo (Yevali) id 1007, Bieria (Vowa) id 1031, Baki id 1033, all from Tryon 1976.
sources.note: No stress marking; used only for the identity check on Fraser 1891.

sources.citation: Fraser, R. M. 1891. Grammar of the Bierian language of the island of Epi, New Hebrides. In D. Macdonald (ed.), South Sea Languages, vol. 2 (Tangoan-Santo, Malo, Malekula, Epi (Baki and Bierian), Tanna, and Futuna), 98-107. Melbourne: Edgerton & Moore.
sources.note: p. 99: 'It is differently accented from the Baki. Though the accent most frequently falls on the penultimate, many words of three syllables are accented on the first, and a number of four-syllabled words are accented on the first and third.' BUT the sketch's pronouns and vocabulary (nagku, aiko, nigana, aira, amai, amunu, niga; sakai 'one', velua 'two', fafine, atamani, vatu, nikambo) match Tryon's Bieria (Vovo) list, not any Bierebo list — this is Bieria (bier1246), misfiled under bier1244 by Glottolog.
Cites Budd 2009 as its sole source; Grambank has no stress features.

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: a new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Canberra.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Nothing on stress. §3.10.3 (p. 103) lists only Tryon 1996a (verb-initial mutation), Codrington 1885a:469-470 'a few scraps', Tryon 1976 wordlists (Tavio, Bonkovia, Burupika, Yevali), Gowers 1976 tree names; summary table p. 106 gives Bierebo phonology 'no', grammar 'no'. Its bibliography files Fraser 1891 'Grammar of Bieriean (Epi)' and cites it under Baki and Bieria, not Bierebo.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1996. Mae-Morae and the languages of Epi (Vanuatu). In Lynch & Pat (eds), Oceanic studies, Pacific Linguistics C-133, 305-318.

sources.note: Same passing 'normal in unstressed position' remark about Proto-Epi realis-marker vowel loss; comparative verb-mutation data from Bonkovia and Yevali; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1986. Stem-initial consonant alternation in the languages of Epi, Vanuatu: a case of assimilation? In FOCAL II, Pacific Linguistics C-94, 239-258.
sources.note: Only a passing remark that loss of the realis-marker vowel 'would be normal in unstressed position' (p. 257); no Bierebo stress rule.
